card.name: Inside pinyin names of Chinese formulas
card.fires_on: Syllables of romanized Chinese (pinyin) names, mostly inside bracketed formula names or journal titles in traditional Chinese medicine texts. It fires on a syllable partway through the name, such as tao, nei, zuo, du or qin.

modes.label: Formula name syllables
modes.description: A pinyin syllable inside the bracketed name of an herbal formula.
modes.example: persica & rhubarb combination (ta<<o>> ren cheng qi tang) is used

modes.label: Classic or journal titles
modes.description: A pinyin syllable inside a Chinese book or journal title.
modes.example: Journal of TCM Internal Medicine (Zh<<ong>> Hua Nei Ke Za Zi)

card.writes: It pushes toward Chinese characters for name-like endings, such as 字, 氏 and 部, which fits a romanized Chinese name context.
card.plain: It marks the middle of a romanized Chinese name, such as an herbal formula or a Chinese journal title.
